limits: I read only the supplied enlarged rows of s116, s118, s120 and s122, without zooming further. This review approves nothing outside these 8 units. Emet veyatziv, elohai netzor and the s124 text are not covered, even though they appear in the same rows.

Across all four pages the print shows a recurring vertical stroke beside penultimate-stress vowels. It is the same glyph the human encoded as meteg in זִכְרֹנֵֽנוּ וּפִקְדֹּנֵֽנוּ. I listed only the occurrences where I actually saw a separate stroke. There are probably more in words I did not list, which is why no unit except adonai_sefatai gets Hebrew approval. Each occurrence needs a human decision on the host letter, made from the native scan.
The dagesh questions in לָּךְ (s116), סֶּלָה ×2 (s116 and s122), לְּךָ and לָּנוּ (s122), and תֵבֵל (s120) remain open from both earlier audits. I neither certify nor reject any of them.

My paragraph-structure findings for gevurot, hodaah and sim_shalom are based on the right-margin indentation in the enlarged rows. Elsewhere on the same pages the encoding follows that indentation consistently.

The missing pb applies to the three modules that cross pages: qedushat_hashem, qedushat_hayom and avodah. The English modules have the same gap. I did not check whether the build tolerates module-level facs for later pages, so I applied the stated rule.
The human decisions in snippets 1-7 were applied as authoritative and not reopened. The other human decision files named in the request concern other pages and units, so I did not consult them.
